subject: Judge F: migrate — drain existing backlog to converge the graph, retire queue-as-default
description:
One-time convergence + retirement of the standing-queue model. Part of the eager-judgment-lifecycle redesign; final step.

DO:
1. Drain the existing ~635-item judge backlog ONCE (using the upgraded neighborhood-aware judge, task A) so the existing graph reaches a fully-judged steady state — every existing candidate edge gets a verdict. After this, the DAG is complete-and-judged for the current corpus, which is the precondition DAG-only consumption (task E) relies on.
2. Retire the standing drain as the DEFAULT path: after convergence, the queue exists ONLY as task D's timeout fallback, not as the primary judgment mechanism. Remove/disable the periodic-drain-as-default nudges (the hourly hook nudge, idle-fill judge_edges) now that judgment is eager (task C). Keep the fallback path.
3. Verify steady state: after drain + eager dispatch live, new nodes get judged on add and the backlog stays ~empty (not re-accumulating).

TEST: post-migration, backlog converges toward 0 and stays there as new nodes are added (eager dispatch keeps up); the timeout-fallback path still functions if a dispatch is starved.

GUARDRAIL: blocked by C + D + E (the full eager+gate+consume mechanism must be live before retiring the queue default). This is where the 635 backlog finally clears for good.
